title: She wasn’t supposed to be there.
paragraphs: She wasn’t supposed to be there.

And that reach?
It broke every rule society placed on her.
Because shame will always try to silence you before grace can reach you.

Twelve years of bleeding.
Twelve years of hiding.
Twelve years of hearing whispers when she walked by… or worse—seeing people step away.

That quiet humiliation.
That invisible label stamped on your life: “Stay back.”

Maybe it’s the sin nobody knows about.
The addiction you keep promising God you’ll quit… but don’t.
The thoughts you’d be ashamed to say out loud.
The version of you that smiles in public but crumbles in private.
And here’s the lie shame keeps repeating:

“You’ve gone too far.”
“You’re too dirty.”
“God helps people better than you.”
So you stay in the crowd.

Close enough to see Jesus…
But never close enough to touch Him.
She was done listening to shame.

She didn’t wait to be invited.
She didn’t clean herself up first.
She didn’t fix her condition before coming.

“And behold, a woman who had suffered from a discharge of blood for twelve years came up behind Him and touched the fringe of His garment, for she said to herself, ‘If I only touch His garment, I will be made well.’ Jesus turned, and seeing her He said, ‘Take heart, daughter; your faith has made you well.’ And instantly the woman was made well.” — Matthew 9:20–22
Because it was never about how strong her grip was.
It was about who she was reaching for.
But here’s what should shake you…

According to the law (Leviticus 15), her condition made her ceremonially unclean.
Anything—or anyone—she touched would also be considered unclean.
She should have made Jesus unclean.
That’s the Gospel hiding in plain sight.

You’ve been afraid to come close because of what you’ve done.
But the very thing you think disqualifies you… is the reason He came.
“For our sake He made Him to be sin who knew no sin, so that in Him we might become the righteousness of God.” — 2 Corinthians 5:21
At the cross, He took your shame, your hidden sin, your private battles—every stain—and bore it fully.
Some scholars interpret this moment with the woman as more than just physical healing—it’s a preview of the cross itself. A Savior who does not withdraw from impurity, but steps into it to redeem.
And when He turned and called her “daughter”…
She went from outcast… to family.
And here’s the part we miss.
In a crowd full of noise, pressure, urgency—He stopped.

That means your quiet prayer?
He hears it.

That hidden struggle?
He sees it.
That moment where you almost gave up?
Faith risks being seen in the middle of shame.
And maybe that’s where you are right now.
Between “What if God rejects me?” and “What if He doesn’t?”
Let me tell you the truth your shame doesn’t want you to hear:
Jesus is not repelled by your brokenness.
But the Gospel goes deeper than healing your situation.
You are not just someone God tolerates.
Through Christ, you become someone God adopts.
“But to all who did receive Him, who believed in His name, He gave the right to become children of God.” — John 1:12
So what are you waiting for?

More guilt?
More hiding?
Another year of pretending you’re fine?

Not when you’re better.
Not when you’ve fixed yourself.
Not when your life looks more “Christian.”

Bring the addiction.
Bring the secret.
Bring the shame you’ve buried so deep you don’t even name it anymore.

Because the same Savior who stopped for her…
Is still stopping for people like you.
And when you reach Him, you won’t just find healing.
You’ll find a Savior who calls you family.
